svg.aria-label: Desktop Material: a commit graph branching inside a rounded tile
svg.title: Desktop Material
svg.desc:
The project's own mark, drawn for this repository rather than inherited.
A Git commit graph — a trunk of two nodes with a third branching away and merging back — set in a Material Design 3 rounded tile. The subject is what the application is for; the tile and the palette are where it lives.
Drawn for 16px first and scaled up, not the other way round. At sixteen pixels a logo is a silhouette: three dots, one trunk, one curve. Everything here is a filled shape or a thick round-capped stroke, there is no detail below about eight units, and nothing relies on a hairline or a gradient surviving the downscale. The two accent nodes stay distinguishable from the trunk by position rather than by hue, so the mark still reads in greyscale and to a colour-blind reader.
Colours are the app's own tokens rather than new ones: --dm-green for the tile, --dm-green-container for the graph, --md-sys-color-primary-container for the branch node. A logo that invents its own palette is a second brand.
